why: A document whose arrival has passed is not supply until somebody re-dates it - once it
is DEAD (later than overdue_dead_days, 90 by policy). R-O (3 Sep 2026) gives a late
document a grace period and lets it count at an assumed date; this case is the far side
of that ruling, where R31 still holds. The document dated 1 April against a walk taken
on 1 September is 153 days late: it contributes NOTHING to the balance and the line it
would have covered is short - but it is returned as uncounted, because a document nobody
mentions reads as a document that is not there, and the buyer has to chase it.
